worlds.name: Almanac
worlds.lineage: The newspaper weather page and its key
worlds.thesis: The day read as a forecast: conditions reported, never praised.
worlds.signature: The daylight band — a 62px night track with a wheat day block from sun-up to sun-down, every timed obligation pinned at its hour as a 27px state circle — plus a permanent four-symbol key (Taken / Waiting / No one / Said no).

worlds.name: Primer
worlds.thesis: Five flat inks and one line: a four-year-old and an adult read the same page.
worlds.signature: The person-token — a flat two-ink glyph (circle, bottom-46% body block in the person's ink, 40% head circle in ink) used at 48px and 30px, with a dashed empty token printing '?' for nobody. Cards carry a flat ink head band tinted by the state's wash, never a coloured side stripe.

worlds.name: Departures
worlds.thesis: Every obligation has a time, a destination and a named driver.
worlds.signature: The status plate — the lead unanswered item raised out of the board with its state word as a plate, the elapsed time since it was asked, a 26px/800 title, and time · place · for whom. Board rows reserve a fixed 84px end column so the right edge stays a straight line.

stateContract.mechanism: Every state is carried by a word, a colour and a shape simultaneously. Word from STATUS_WORD in src/domain/rules.ts; colour from --s-*/--s-*-wash; shape from .mark--* plus dashed-vs-solid edges. Marks ship role="img" with the status word as aria-label.

departures.note: state word inverts to solid amber on #241803

states.shape: solid circle with a drawn check at stroke 3

departures.note: state word inverts to solid cyan on #06272b

states.shape: solid circle with a drawn cross at stroke 3

narrative.overview:
One family record, set three times by three different print shops. The domain, the flows and every shared component are written once; data-world on .phone swaps a complete token fill, and the same list of obligations comes out as a newspaper weather page, a mid-century picture book, or a departures board. The three worlds are peers. None is a theme of another, and none is a colour variant: they differ in type, ground, density, line weight, corner language and signature move.

The product is read by six-year-olds and by adults in the same minute, so legibility is solved structurally rather than stylistically. No world softens into cartoon. Every state is printed as a word and a colour and a shape at the same time, so the screen survives greyscale, a colour-blind parent and a pre-reader. "Nobody has this" is a material — 45° hatching and a dashed edge — not an absence. Icons are one drawn 24-box SVG set at 1.75 stroke; there are no emoji and no font glyphs anywhere in the product.

Density is phone-native and unapologetically informational: 390×844, a flat scrolling column under a world masthead, a 76px tab bar, and rows that carry time, state, owner and place without a card around them (except in Primer, where the card is the row). Decoration is near zero; what looks like ornament — the daylight band, the key, the status plate — is always reporting data.
keyCharacteristics: Three complete worlds behind one token contract, switched at runtime
State = word + colour + shape, always, simultaneously
Hatching and a dashed edge mean "open / nobody"
One drawn SVG icon set, 1.75 stroke, 24-box; no emoji, no glyph fonts
Flat informational density; type does the hierarchy, not elevation
Light grounds for the two reading worlds, near-black for the glance world

rules.name: The Three-Carrier Rule
rules.body: Every state — unowned, waiting, accepted, declined, asked-out, handled — is carried by a word (STATUS_WORD in src/domain/rules.ts: No one / Waiting / Taken / Said no / Asked out / Handled), a colour (--s-*), and a shape (.mark--*, and dashed vs. solid edges) at the same time. No state may ever be carried by colour alone, in any world, on any surface. The audit test: desaturate the screen and read it; if a state became unreadable, the surface is wrong.

rules.name: The Hatch Rule
rules.body: 45° hatching (--hatch) plus a dashed edge means "open — the record has no owner". It is the texture of unowned in every world: the mark, the empty person mark, the Almanac pin, the Primer card band. Hatching is never decorative, and never used for anything else.

rules.name: The Wash Pairing Rule
rules.body: A state ink is never used as a fill behind text. Each --s-* ink ships with an --s-*-wash ground, and that pair is the only legal combination — except in Departures, where waiting deliberately inverts to solid amber with departures-on-amber text because the glance screen wants one siren.

rules.name: The Tabular Column Rule
rules.body: Any number that sits in a column — clock times, day numbers, elapsed counts, the message timestamp — carries .tnum (font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums). Times must not shift width between rows.

rules.name: The No-Shouting-In-Primer Rule
rules.body: Uppercase tracked micro-type is Almanac's and Departures' voice. In Primer, [data-world='primer'] resets every label, divider, tab and state word to sentence case — because a picture book sets its captions, it does not stamp them.

rules.name: The Lede Rule
rules.body: Every masthead carries one line of what is actually true right now, in body size, capped at 28–32ch, with the single most important noun in <b> and the world's accent colour. One bold phrase per lede, never two.

rules.name: The One-Column Rule
rules.body: There is no multi-column layout and no responsive breakpoint in this product. Everything is one 390px column; density is solved by row height, not by splitting the page.

rules.name: The Flat-Row Rule
rules.body: A list row never lifts. .row:hover and .dep-row:hover change background only, and an unanswered row is marked by a wash (.row--open → --s-waiting-wash), never by elevation.

rules.name: The Tone-Over-Lift Rule
rules.body: When a surface needs to read as a different plane, change its ground (--surface-2, --surface-sunk, a state wash) and give it a rule. Handled is a destination, so the whole screen takes --s-handled-wash as its ground; it does not take a shadow.

rules.name: The Dashed-Edge Rule
rules.body: A dashed border means unowned. It appears on .state--unowned, .mark--unowned, .person--none, .alm-pin--unowned and .pri-token.is-empty, and nowhere else.

dos: Do print every state with its word, its colour and its shape at once — STATUS_WORD for the word, --s-* for the colour, .mark--* or a dashed edge for the shape.
Do take the state word from STATUS_WORD (No one / Waiting / Taken / Said no / Asked out / Handled). A world may lengthen it into a sentence ("Waiting on Taylor"), never rename the state.
Do style a new shared component entirely from the token contract (--ink, --surface, --rule, --line, --r-*, --s-*, --font-*), so it works in all three worlds unseen.
Do put world-specific overrides behind [data-world='…'] in the shared stylesheet or in the world's own CSS file.
Do give every interactive control a box of at least 44px (.iconBtn 44px, .btn 46px, .input 46px, .check__row 46px, .pickRow 60px).
Do mark hatching + a dashed edge as the only way to say "nobody has this".
Do draw new icons into src/ui/Icon.tsx on the 24 box at 1.75 stroke with round caps and joins.
Do add .tnum to any number that sits in a column.
Do keep the three motion durations and let them collapse to 1ms under reduced motion.
Do cap a lede at 28–32ch and bold exactly one phrase in it.
Do use color-mix(in srgb, …) against an existing token for a hover darkening, rather than introducing a new hex.
donts: Don't let colour alone carry a state, a count, or an owner — not in a dot, not in a stripe, not in a bar.
Don't ship an emoji or an icon-font glyph. Every glyph in the product comes from the drawn set.
Don't give a Primer card a coloured side stripe or a rounded corner; that world states colour as a flat head band at region scale and keeps every corner at 0px.
Don't soften a radius to signal friendliness. The radius belongs to the world (--r-*); legibility is the all-ages mechanism, roundness is not.
Don't lift a list row, a header, a key or a plate on hover. Change its ground.
Don't mix a state ink with a surface other than its paired --s-*-wash.
Don't add a fourth ink step, a fifth person colour, or a second accent to a world.
Don't collapse, hide or shorten the Almanac key — it is permanent and four-symbol.
Don't replace a bottom sheet with a blocking centred modal.
Don't remove a focus ring or borrow another world's ring colour.
Don't introduce a hex literal in a component stylesheet; the only shared literals in the product are #fff on a state fill and the sheet backdrop.
Don't treat the device frame or the world/role rig (frame.css) as part of the product's visual system.
